subject: D2A37FC072734EADAA2D0F4A2BC2B5B0
introduction: A community, in this guide, is made by people who love one another, meet often, consult, write to each other, teach their children, help other communities and build together a place of worship; and its institutions exist to serve that life. The eighty-six quotations are read here with eighty-six from elsewhere. Much comes from the letters of Paul, who spent his life forming such communities and writing to them: one body with many members, the same mind, bearing one another’s burdens, not forsaking the assembly. Acts shows the first believers of one heart and one soul; the Qur’an tells believers to hold together and take counsel; Confucius delights in friends from afar; Hillel says not to separate from the community; Tocqueville and Burke describe the associations and little platoons in which public affection begins. The cautions are from Pascal and the Dhammapada, who know the worth of solitude; from Emerson, for whom society conspires against the individual; from Madison, on why order is needed; and from Paul, Kabir and the Gospel of John on whether God needs a house at all.
questions: The guide calls love among the members the one essential. What practices in the readings turn that love into habits a community can keep?
Pascal and the Dhammapada value solitude, and Emerson distrusts society. What does a healthy community leave room for in each member?
The guide says administration is an instrument and not an end. How can a community tell when its structures have begun to serve themselves?
Paul and Kabir say God does not dwell in buildings, and the guide attaches great importance to a house of worship. What can a shared building do that nothing else does?
Several readings ask communities in different lands to help one another. What does a local community gain from belonging to a wider one?
One reading says believers have not yet learned to draw on each other's love for strength. What would learning that look like where you live?

outside.why: Jesus makes the same thing the one mark of his disciples: that they have love one to another.
Paul pictures a body fitly joined together, which grows by what every joint supplies, to the edifying of itself in love.
Hebrews gives the purpose of assembling: to consider one another, to provoke unto love and to good works.
Paul tells a mixed church that they are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens and of the household of God.
Hebrews asks its readers not to be forgetful to entertain strangers, since some have entertained angels unawares.
Paul's image for many who are one is the body, which is one and has many members.
Donne holds that no man is an island: every man is a piece of the continent, a part of the main.
Proverbs says that where no counsel is the people fall, but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.
The Qur'an describes the faithful as those whose affairs are a matter of counsel among them.
Paul speaks of laying a foundation as a wise masterbuilder, and warns each to take heed how he builds on it.
Paul asks his friends to comfort themselves together and edify one another, as they are already doing.
In the parable the shepherd leaves the ninety and nine and goes after the one that is lost until he finds it.
Isaiah's shepherd gathers the lambs with his arm, carries them in his bosom and gently leads those with young.
Jesus says that one who remembers a quarrel should leave the gift before the altar and first be reconciled.
Jesus warns that every city or house divided against itself shall not stand.
The Qur'an says that the believers are naught else than brothers, and asks that peace be made between them.
Paul asks a church to do all things without murmurings and disputings, shining as lights in the world.
The elder too has more to say than ink will carry, and hopes to speak face to face.
Jesus likens the kingdom to leaven which a woman hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.
The Preacher says that two are better than one, for if they fall the one will lift up his fellow, and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
Pascal traced all the unhappiness of men to one fact, that they cannot stay quietly in their own chamber. Is the wish always to be together a strength, or can it be a flight from oneself?
Paul names the fruits a fellowship should bear: love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness.
The psalm exclaims how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity.
The Qur'an tells believers to hold fast, all together, to the cable of God, and not to separate.
Confucius says that virtue is not left to stand alone: he who practises it will have neighbours.
Proverbs compares good news from a far country to cold waters to a thirsty soul.
Jesus blesses the peacemakers, and says they shall be called the children of God.
Paul asks believers to rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep.
Paul writes to a church he cannot visit that he is with them in the spirit, joying and beholding their order.
Proverbs says that iron sharpeneth iron, so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
Malachi says that they that feared the Lord spake often one to another, and the Lord hearkened and heard.
Jesus promises to be in the midst wherever two or three are gathered together in his name.
Jesus says that the sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath.
The psalmist was glad when they said unto him, let us go into the house of the Lord.
Confucius asks whether it is not delightful to have friends coming from distant quarters.
Jesus tells his disciples not to forbid one who does good outside their company: he that is not against us is on our part.
The Lord's Prayer asks that the will be done in earth as it is in heaven.
Acts says of the first community that the multitude of them that believed were of one heart and of one soul.
Luke names the women who travelled with Jesus and the twelve and ministered to them of their substance.
Paul commends Phebe, a servant of the church, and asks that she be received and helped in whatever she needs.
A letter of Paul says that women are to keep silence in the churches. What does it change, for a community, when its women hold their own gatherings and teach?
Wollstonecraft argued that to strengthen the female mind by enlarging it would put an end to blind obedience.
Proverbs gives the reason for every school: train up a child in the way he should go.
Paul asks that his letter be read in one church and passed on to the next.
Paul asks one church to supply another's want from its abundance, so that in turn there may be equality.
Paul gives mutual help as a law: bear ye one another's burdens.
The Qur'an commands: help ye one another unto righteousness and pious duty.
The apostles ask the whole multitude to look out seven men of honest report to take charge of a practical need.
Paul pleads with a church to be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.
Madison wrote that if men were angels no government would be necessary. What does a community's need for principles of order say about its members, and what does it not say?
Zechariah hears how small beginnings succeed: not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit.
Tocqueville observed that Americans constantly form associations of a thousand kinds, serious and futile, enormous and diminutive.
Proverbs says that without counsel purposes are disappointed, but in the multitude of counsellors they are established.
Isaiah foresees the wilderness glad, and the desert rejoicing and blossoming as the rose.
Isaiah foresees a people who build the old wastes and repair the waste cities, the desolations of many generations.
Proverbs passes the field of the slothful and finds it all grown over with thorns.
The psalmist's soul longs and even faints for the courts of the Lord.
Paul told his hearers that the Lord of heaven and earth dwelleth not in temples made with hands. What can a building do for worship, if God is not housed in it?
Kabir's God says: I am beside thee, I am neither in temple nor in mosque. If that is so, what is a house of worship for?
Isaiah hears that the house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.
Jesus tells a Samaritan woman that the hour comes when worship will be neither on her mountain nor at Jerusalem, but in spirit and in truth. What makes a place a centre without making it a boundary?
Solomon says of the house he has built that heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain the one it is for.
Paul thanks God that the faith of one city's believers is spoken of throughout the whole world.
Jesus calls his followers the light of the world, a city set on an hill that cannot be hid.
Daniel says that they that turn many to righteousness shall shine as the stars for ever and ever.
Paul uses the image of fragrance: the savour of the knowledge of God made manifest in every place.
Jesus says to a small company of followers: fear not, little flock, and promises them the kingdom.
Jesus likens the kingdom to a mustard seed, the least of all seeds, which becomes the greatest among herbs.
Jacob dreams of a ladder set up on the earth whose top reaches to heaven, with angels ascending and descending.
Paul asks that as we have opportunity we do good unto all men.
Jesus says that even a cup of cold water given to one of the little ones shall not lose its reward.
Aristotle distinguishes a whole that is something besides its parts from a mere heap.
Burke held that to love the little platoon we belong to in society is the first principle of public affections.
Emerson says that society everywhere is in conspiracy against the manhood of every one of its members. What must a community be like for that not to be true of it?
Hillel taught: do not separate yourself from the community, and do not trust in yourself until the day of your death.
Paul warns those who serve a community that the letter kills, but the spirit gives life.
Mill held that the worth of a State, in the long run, is the worth of the individuals composing it.
Acts describes a community continuing daily with one accord, breaking bread from house to house with gladness.
The Dhammapada advises a traveller who meets no better or equal to keep firmly to his solitary journey. When is it right to stand apart from the company one has?
Paul tells each member to use the gift given, whether prophecy, ministry, teaching or exhortation.
Jesus tells his disciples to come apart into a desert place and rest a while. What do times of withdrawal together give a community that its ordinary life does not?
Paul says that if one member suffer, all the members suffer with it, and if one be honoured, all rejoice.
Paul asks for lowliness, meekness and longsuffering, forbearing one another in love, endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit.
Jesus says: take no thought for the morrow, for sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.
Paul ends his chapter on love by saying that faith, hope and charity abide, and the greatest of these is charity.
John's letter says that love is of God, and every one that loveth is born of God and knoweth God.

ephesians-endeavouring-to-keep-the-unity.text: I therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, beseech you that ye walk worthy of the vocation wherewith ye are called, With all lowliness and meekness, with longsuffering, forbearing one another in love; Endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace

ecclesiastes-two-are-better-than-one.text: Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up. Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone? And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken

ephesians-no-more-strangers.text: Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God

acts-seven-men-of-honest-report.text: Then the twelve called the multitude of the disciples unto them, and said, It is not reason that we should leave the word of God, and serve tables. Wherefore, brethren, look ye out among you seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business. But we will give ourselves continually to prayer, and to the ministry of the word

matthew-take-no-thought-for-the-morrow.text: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof

corinthians-if-one-member-suffer.text: That there should be no schism in the body; but that the members should have the same care one for another. And whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it; or one member be honoured, all the members rejoice with it

romans-your-faith-is-spoken-of.text: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world

dhammapada-solitary-journey.text: If a traveller does not meet with one who is his better, or his equal, let him firmly keep to his solitary journey; there is no companionship with a fool
